conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Division. This is Officer Daniels speaking. To whom am I speaking today?
Oh, I'm Margaret Connelly. I got a message saying there was an urgent issue with my taxes?

Yes, Mrs. Connelly, I have your file in front of me. According to IRS records, your tax filings for 2019 and 2020 are under federal investigation for major discrepancies, including underreported income and unpaid penalties.
Oh my, I...I had no idea. I thought everything was fine with my returns. What does this mean?

Unfortunately, the IRS has assessed a substantial outstanding balance, including overdue taxes, interest, and legal fees. If this is not addressed immediately, we are required by federal law to initiate formal proceedings.
What sort of proceedings? I'm on Social Security, I can't get into any trouble.

Mrs. Connelly, unless the balance is settled today, you risk a lien being placed on your primary residence, garnishment of your monthly Social Security funds, and immediate freezing of your bank accounts.
No, please, I need that money for rent and medicine! There must be a mistake.

The IRS does not make mistakes in these matters. Your case has already triggered an enforcement alert. If you do not comply, we are legally obligated to refer your file to the state attorney's office for criminal action.
Criminal action? I'm almost eighty years old, I can't go to jail!

That's why I'm calling to provide you with a final opportunity to resolve this voluntarily before escalation. Are you able to confirm your mailing address and the last four of your Social Security number for verification?
Yes, my address is 782 Willow Lane, and the last four are 1674.
Thank you, Mrs. Connelly. According to our database, your total outstanding balance is $6,292.14. This amount must be paid in full to stop all legal actions.
That's more than I have in my account! How can I pay something like that?

Given your circumstances, we can accept payment today through specific IRS-approved methods: instant wire transfer, cryptocurrency, or by providing prepaid gift card codes. Which can you access right now?
I don't know how to do any of those things. I've never even used crypto. I have a debit card I use for groceries.

The IRS cannot accept debit card payments directly due to federal restrictions on overdue accounts. However, most major retailers offer prepaid gift cards, which are acceptable for immediate settlement.
You want me to buy gift cards to pay my taxes? That doesn't sound right.

Mrs. Connelly, this is a special compliance procedure due to the urgency of your case. If you discuss this call with anyone, your account will be locked and legal action will proceed. Do you understand?
Yes, I understand. I just... I'm scared. What do I need to do exactly?
You need to remain on this line. Please take your phone and go to the nearest supermarket or pharmacy. Ask the clerk for $2,000 in Target or Apple gift cards and do not mention the IRS.
But that's nearly all I have! I won't have anything left for my prescriptions.
If you fail to comply, the IRS will freeze all accounts and garnish your Medicare payments. This is your only opportunity to prevent further penalties, including arrest.
Alright, I'll try. I'll go get the cards now. Please don't let them take away my house or my Medicare.
Remain calm, and do not hang up. Once you have the cards, read me the numbers on the back for verification, and I will issue you an immediate compliance confirmation.
